title: The Slaves' Proposal
text: “Long time no see, how’s business?”
“Word is the Waves are coming, so it’s slow going.”
“That’s a relief, in a way.”
“So, I’ve been hearing rumors about you and your crew, Little Miss…”
The weapon shop owner shifted his gaze to the half-breed Lizardman and Rabbit Man standing behind Father, along with Wolf.
“Ah… lots of things happened, and now I’m doing odd jobs for a slave trader and managing a circus business. Thanks to that, I got some slaves supplied to me as manpower.”
Father answered with a hint of self-deprecation.
“Even with the Spear guy still around?”
“Well, that’s… complicated too. There’s a story behind it.”
“Sounds like a job I can’t really approve of.”
The shop owner frowned, and the Rabbit Man stepped forward with an indignant expression.
“No, it’s not a bad job at all. Thanks to it, I got to meet Iwatani-sama, and honestly, the environment is quite good.”
“O-oh?”

“That look says you doubt I’m being forced to say this. Not at all. Thanks to Iwatani-sama, my skills have improved tremendously, and I’m learning everything—knowledge, combat techniques, all of it. There are practically no unreasonable orders.”
“Hold on, Theo.”
The Rabbit Man placed a hand on the counter with a gesture eerily similar to something I myself might do, indeed.
“So then, Iwatani-sama, what were you planning to purchase at this weapon shop today?”
“Umm… I’m not quite sure why you’re so concerned about what I’m buying, Theo, but…”
Seeing this exchange, the shop owner burst out laughing.
“Hahaha! That’s one lively bunch of companions you’ve got there. Wouldn’t know they were slaves if you didn’t tell me.”
“Yes, quite true indeed.”
“…Keep it in moderation. It’s a problem when the sense of tension disappears entirely.”
The half-breed Lizardman cautioned the Rabbit Man with a sigh.
“Vau.”
Meanwhile, Wolf scratched his fur with a hind leg, thoroughly relaxed.
“So, what are you planning to buy?”
The half-breed Lizardman asked Father while examining an axe in the weapons corner of the shop.
“Well, I’d like to get a full set of weapons and armor for everyone.”
“And you?”
“What about you, Iwatani-sama?”
“Kuun?”
The slaves all turned their eyes to Father in unison.
“I figure the leather armor I already picked up should be fine for me.”

Equipment usable in Melromarc was rather limited, I say. Which meant Father was simply going to keep cycling through gear looted from Three Heroes Church bandits. Incidentally, though inspectors frequently came around asking after the whereabouts of those very bandits, contact was impossible since they’d all been enslaved over in Siltvelt. A fitting reward for their self-righteous brand of justice, indeed.
“Rejected. Hey, get the best gear our funds can buy for this guy.”
“Agreed. Please prioritize this over our own weapons and armor.”
“Vau vau!”
The half-breed Lizardman grabbed Father by the shoulder from behind and dragged him to the counter, with the Rabbit Man and Wolf following close behind.
“Hold on, do you two even remember who the master is here?”
“Doesn’t matter. I’ve thought this for a while now—no matter how sturdy you are, that’s no excuse to neglect yourself.”
“Yes, Iwatani-sama, you’re the Hero who commands all of us, you know? You really ought to value yourself more, or who knows what might happen during a Wave.”
Big Sister seemed to be saying something along the lines of scolding Father as well.
“Normally, you’re the one who should be equipped with the very best. If the leader throws himself in as a shield and dies for it, it’s the ones he protected who end up in trouble.”

The half-breed Lizardman’s tone carried unusual weight as he lectured Father rather sternly. Father apparently sensed, somehow, what lay behind those words. Éclair’s parent, it seemed, had died fighting at the front lines during a Wave, defending the townsfolk during an evacuation. That, presumably, was what he meant.
“So no matter what happens, you must never pull something that gets you killed. Which is why we settle your equipment first.”
“Wau!”
“…Yeah, yeah, I get it. Honestly…”
Looking thoroughly exasperated, Father coughed lightly and ended up asking the grinning shop owner to arrange his equipment first.
“Good to see you all getting along so well, eh?”
“It’s a struggle to maintain any dignity around here, honestly.”
“Suits you fine, if you ask me. The Shield Hero’s whole role is about valuing his companions, and I’d say being cherished like this is about the best thing that could happen.”
“I suppose that’s true… well then, since my equipment’s apparently first priority, let’s figure out what to do.”
Father’s wry smile simply wouldn’t fade. While that exchange played out, I turned my attention aside to check on Yuki-chan and Kuro-chan, indeed.
“Waah, the Dark Swordsman… a single flashing slash gleaming in the night…”
Kuro-chan struck a pose, gripping a sword displayed on a shelf.
“Hmm…”
Somehow, it just didn’t seem to click for Kuro-chan. Come to think of it, I still hadn’t managed to introduce Ren. Not that I’d forgotten, mind you, I say.
“Being a beloved leader is important, you know. Yuki thinks Yuki should aim to be the kind of leader everyone looks up to and brings proposals to, but it’s proving rather difficult.”
“All the Filolials like being carefree and having fun, so I bet they all adore you, Yuki-chan. A reliable leader, right? Right, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Indeed. Thanks to Yuki-chan, we’ve been saved more than once, I say.”
“Yuki will try even harder!”
“Hey Yuki, whaddya think of this?”
“Kuro should keep the obsession with looking cool in moderation. Wielding a sword well is difficult enough as it is.”
Kuro-chan appeared to be researching just how to hold a sword in the coolest possible way.
“I still think doing it like Grandpa did—zubababa!—looks way cooler! Like Whirlwind Wing <Tornado Cooking>, pinching the kitchen knife just like that!”

Whirlwind Wing <Tornado Cooking> was the nickname Kuro-chan had bestowed upon Panda’s foster father. Kuro-chan’s eyes had positively sparkled watching Panda’s foster father perform his acrobatic cooking alongside Father, indeed. It was a flashy style of cooking, quite different from the acrobatics Ark and Father did together, and it had drawn its own crowd of customers.
“So, how much are we working with, funds-wise?”
Ah, here came the talk of war funds. Father signaled with a finger as if wanting to have a private word, then beckoned me over. Which meant the secret conversation would be just the three of us.
“In terms of money usable domestically, all told, I can put up more than thirty gold coins.”

Ohh… truly impressive, Father—earning so widely and handsomely through the circus business as war funds, indeed. Lately, on Lazy Pig’s suggestion, there’d also been the food stalls. Which tied right into what Kuro-chan had just mentioned. That side of things was apparently thriving enough to bring in plenty of earnings. What’s more, Panda’s foster father was pitching in as help there too. Word had spread, and even customers from Zeltoble’s underground culinary scene were reportedly lining up to eat. With the flashy cooking performed at the stall drawing showers of tips, the whole operation was booming, I say. If only I could arrange to arrive during a time period similar to this loop, perhaps I could have Father run the food stall together with Panda’s foster father as an activity of their own.
“Ugh… I’ve got a chill running down my spine for some reason.”
“Caught a cold, perhaps?”
Father, if you’re tired, please do rest properly, I say.
“No… I think it’s just my imagination. Since I’m earning way too much, I figure gear in the three-gold-coin range should do fine.”
“Ain’t you been rakin’ it in for such a short stretch of time, Little Miss.”

Well, when it came to peddling goods, everything from gathering herbs to the rest had all been handmade and self-managed, after all. Running a circus business with a full staff to manage was bound to be a different story entirely, profitable or not, given the circumstances. As for the purchase costs of the slaves—those had, in fact, already been settled via Siltvelt. Trading in captured bandits was turning out to be quite the lucrative business indeed.
